Wedding bells are ringing for Miley Cyrus and her fiancé, Maxx Morando.

The rockers are planning to say “I do” in a ceremony in Southern California this weekend, according to a TMZ source.

The news of their engagement was first confirmed in September 2025, after Cyrus was seen wearing a sparkling engagement ring as they posed together on the red carpet at the premiere of “Avatar: Fire and Ash.”.

Sources indicate that cyrus, 33, and Morando, 28, have been linked since the summer of 2021. In a British Vogue cover interview, the “Flowers” singer recalled their introduction, explaining, “We got put on a blind date.”.

According to recent reports, she then provided a key clarifying detail, noting, “Well, it was blind for me and not really for him. I thought, ‘The worst that can happen is I leave.’”.

It’s safe to say the date was a success, with their love story blossoming over the last four years.

Almost immediately, they began collaborating together professionally, with Cyrus telling Vogue Morando was one of her “favorite emerging artists,” having designed sustainable looks for her to wear during her various appearances in music festivals in 2021.

Later that year, Morando’s band, Liily, performed as part of “Miley’s Latest Year’s Eve Party,” where the “Hannah Montana” star rang in the New Year with an NBC special.

He’s even collaborated on some of Cyrus’s most recent music, and in a Harper’s Bazaar interview, she explained the significance of bringing a romantic partner into her professional sphere.

“I worked with my dad forever. That’s how me and my ex-husband met each other,” she mentioned. “I’ve always worked with the people that I love. And Maxx just inspires me so much.”.

While Morando appears to be quite private in regards to his personal life, he has publicly supported his soon-to-be wife at a handful of public events, including movie premieres and award shows.

A few years into their relationship, the nearlyweds took a major leap. A People magazine source confirmed they had moved in together in February 2024.

“She is very happy with him,” the source revealed. “Miley has changed a lot in the past couple of years. She seems more calm and harmonious. Everyone loves Maxx. He’s a great guy. She is very happy with him. He’s private and doesn’t like being in the press. It’s been good for her.”.

Cyrus shared what it’s like to live with her fiance in a September 2026 chat on the Zane Lowe Show, where she gushed that even life’s most mundane tasks are more fun with Morando around.

I think that’s the thing that maybe generations prior didn’t teach us, that marriage doesn’t need to be a prison. It can actually be a playground,” she noted. “It’s just living with a best friend. And that’s what it is.”.

In 2024, an Us magazine source confirmed that although “Miley owns a number of properties,” the lovebirds are “staying at her home in Malibu,” which was described as a “huge mansion overlooking the water in a gated community.”.

According to recent reports, although Cyrus also has homes in Studio City, Hidden Hills, and her home state of Tennessee, the couple reportedly adores the Malibu home’s proximity to the sea. Apparently, they “spend a lot of time on the private beach together.”.

Cyrus has a long history of living in Malibu—and even has a song named after the coastal locale.

According to recent reports, back in 2016, she paid $2.5 million for a gorgeous midcentury modern home in the area. At the time, she shared the 1,385-square-foot dwelling with her now-ex-husband, Liam Hemsworth. The former couple used it as a creative studio and guest house.

The funky home was perched on a two-acre property with lots of lush greenery, which could be peacefully enjoyed from the terrace of the primary bedroom, according to Architectural Digest.

The singer and “The Hunger Games” star would call another Malibu mansion their home, however—a $6.8 million property Hemsworth had purchased in 2014, which was tragically destroyed by the 2018 Wolsey Fire just weeks before their wedding.

In a recent development, the sprawling property was more than just a home. It also housed Rainbowland, her personal recording studio.

Miley reflected on the tragedy in 2025, telling People, “When my house burned down, that was the biggest blessing I’ve ever had in my life, actually.”.

She explained that after “losing everything,” having the opportunity “to rebuild” inspired her to be more “purposeful” when carefully selecting newly introduced belongings.

Cyrus and Hemsworth separated in August 2019, and their divorce was finalized in January 2020.

In the months following the split, Cyrus offloaded the guesthouse at a loss in an off-market transaction for $1.7 million, and Hemsworth sold the wildfire-damaged property for $3.6 million.

In a recent development, it wouldn’t be too long before the “Black Mirror” actress would find herself back in Malibu. She snapped up a $7.9 million Mediterranean mansion in the city in 2022, which is reportedly where she and Morando live now.

The 1999-built property is on a 1.48-acre-lot in a gated community, which affords lots of privacy.

It’s truly a resort-like retreat, with a pool and spa in the backyard surrounded by soaring palm trees.

Indoors, an open-blueprint layout boasts tall ceilings and glass sliding doors that connect the serene space to the equally-tranquil landscape.

The massive primary suite provides striking panoramic views of the beach, and has a lounge space, a fireplace, and a balcony.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Solana has officially removed the "beta" tag from its mainnet's name and introduced the Solana 1.0 standard. The switch was declared on Nov. 16 at the Breakpoint conference in London.

"Solana 1.0 marks the network's graduation from 'mainnet beta' to 'mainnet,' retiring the beta designation it has carried since launch," the Solana Foundation said.

According to recent reports, solana launched on March 16, 2020, and the network had been working under the "mainnet-beta" label for six years and eight months. According to the foundation, the label "never evolved to signal its production status.".

The Solana Foundation coordinated the rollout with the Anza and Firedancer teams. Co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko replied to the announcement on X with three exploding-head emojis.

"For owners, this is the same network, nothing changes. Your SOL, accounts, assets, applications, and transaction history remain the same," the foundation wrote. On Monday, SOL is trading at $71.35.

According to the foundation, two upgrades made the change possible. In October, Solana activated Alpenglow with the Agave 4.3 release, and the time to final confirmation went down by almost 99%, from 12.8 seconds to around 150 milliseconds.

In a recent development, firedancer, a validator client developed by Jump Crypto independently from Agave, is also now running on the Solana mainnet. Independent implementations "limit the impact of bugs affecting one client, and strengthen network resilience," the foundation remarked.

Solana 1.0 also gives the network a shared protocol version, and it does not depend on the version numbers of individual clients such as Agave and Firedancer.

Recent findings suggest that "A shared protocol version lets everyone refer to Solana's evolution without using one client's release number as shorthand for the entire network," the Solana Foundation explained. "Announcing a protocol version does not activate every associated improvement at once.".

Earlier this year, Solana raised the compute limit per block from 60 million to 100 million compute units in May, and the slot time went down from 400 to 200 milliseconds in August. The maximum transaction size also went up from 1,232 to 4,096 bytes.

"Documentation, websites, explorers, and other ecosystem surfaces will progressively reflect the updated designation," the foundation added.

Tech Roundup: Zillow Preview listings go live in RealScout

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, can AI time savings be measured?
  • This week’s Inman Tech Roundup covers Lofty’s new monthly index, which tallies how much time its AI saves agents, a $1.65 billion October for proptech funding, Airbnb’s early-2027 launch window for its AI travel agent and Zillow Preview’s new home inside RealScout.
  • According to recent reports, lofty is launching the Lofty AI Index for Real Estate, a monthly report tracking how much time its AI tools save real estate agents.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, can AI time savings be measured? Lofty is trying. Plus: $1.65 billion in October proptech funding, Airbnb’s AI travel agent and Zillow Preview in RealScout.

This week’s Inman Tech Roundup covers Lofty’s new monthly index, which tallies how much time its AI saves agents, a $1.65 billion October for proptech funding, Airbnb’s early-2027 launch window for its AI travel agent and Zillow Preview’s new home inside RealScout.

According to recent reports, lofty is launching the Lofty AI Index for Real Estate, a monthly report tracking how much time its AI tools save real estate agents. The inaugural edition found Lofty AI products, including Lofty Cowork, completed 1.13 million tasks in October, saving real estate agents 131,248 hours.

The index counts tasks Lofty’s AI completed, such as follow-ups, social media posts, homeowner check-ins and CRM updates, then estimates how long each would take an agent to do manually.

Among the findings: 387,824 leads got an AI follow-up text or email; solo agents saved 30 percent of their hours on daily planning; and agents in Michigan saved more time than any other region.

Sources indicate that “Every AI vendor touts the time-saving nature of their AI product, but almost none of them show the data to confirm that what they say is true. We decided to cut through the smoke and mirrors around AI results and create measurable clarity with the Lofty AI Index. Each month we’ll put a number to the AI impact, show the calculations and stand behind it,” remarked Joe Chen, CEO of Lofty.

According to recent reports, the time-saved figures rest on the organization’s own estimates of manual task times, and the release doesn’t say how many agents are behind the totals, which makes per-agent impact hard to gauge. Since this is the first edition, there’s no prior month to compare against yet.

Sources indicate that for real estate agents weighing AI tools, Lofty’s index is a step toward the kind of hard numbers the industry has been missing. It gives them a benchmark to press other vendors on when they make time-saving claims.

However, the most useful measure is their own: tracking whether hours freed up by AI actually turn into more conversations, listings and closings.

Note: Lofty is the official AI partner of Inman.

Proptech companies raised about $1.65 billion across 34 funding rounds in October, according to the Center for Real Estate Technology & Innovation (CRETI), which called it one of the strongest months of 2026.

In a recent development, the money was heavily concentrated. Construction and development took roughly $872.4 million, or 52.8 percent of the total, while residential pulled in $604.4 million, or 36.6 percent. Three deals alone accounted for nearly 75 percent of October capital: Bedrock Robotics’ $600 million Series C, Unlock’s $433.1 million debt financing and ICON’s $200 million Series D.

Debt was a major part of the story. About $588.6 million, more than a third of the month’s total, came through debt rounds. That includes Unlock’s financing for its home-equity agreement platform and CrowdProperty’s roughly $133.5 million round for residential development lending.

That means much of October’s residential funding didn’t go into software at all but into financial products tied to home equity and property lending.

CRETI noted that funding signals investor conviction, not proof of ROI, and remarked the bar for founders is rising to show a credible link between their technology and a material financial outcome.

The numbers suggest investors are betting less on latest real estate agent-facing software and more on the expensive, physical end of housing, such as building homes faster and cheaper and financing the transactions around them.

If that capital pays off, the bigger impact on agents and brokers may come indirectly, through more housing supply and latest ways for homeowners to tap equity, rather than through the tools on their desks.

Airbnb prepares to roll out its AI travel agent to consumers in the first half of 2027, the firm stated in its third-quarter shareholder letter, firming up a timeline it had previously pegged only as sometime in the next year.

In a recent development, instead of a text-heavy chatbot, the AI agent will assemble a custom interface around each guest’s request, pulling from hundreds of travel-specific components such as maps, photos, comparisons, calendars and itineraries. It will also handle post-booking tasks like reservation changes, refunds, rebooking and payment challenges, which Airbnb argues outside AI agents can’t easily do.

CEO Brian Chesky told analysts that general-purpose AI agents are fine for routine tasks but not for trip planning.

“Travel is aspirational,” Chesky said. “Discovering where to go and where to stay is part of the experience.”.

According to recent reports, the announcement came alongside a strong third quarter for Airbnb. Revenue grew 19 percent year over year to $4.87 billion, beating Wall Street estimates. Airbnb raised its 2026 growth forecast to the high teens, up from the mid-teens. Chesky called it the company’s fastest revenue growth in more than three years.

Airbnb’s bet is one real estate portals and brokerages are weighing, too: that owning the search experience and the transaction behind it beats handing consumers off to general-purpose AI agents.

If a custom, visual AI agent wins over travelers, it’ll strengthen the case for real estate platforms to build their own AI home-search tools rather than relying on outside chatbots to send them buyers.

RealScout is now showing Zillow Preview listings from hundreds of participating brokerages in its collaborative home search platform, putting pre-MLS inventory in front of buyers searching with their own agents.

The integration, first unveiled in September, extends Zillow Preview’s reach beyond Zillow, Trulia and Realtor.com to RealScout’s network of more than 100,000 agents.

Preview listings appear in client searches and listing alerts that include Coming Soon properties. Buyers can message their agent directly about a home, and each Preview listing is replaced by its MLS listing once the home goes active. Agents and brokerages don’t need to opt in to see eligible listings.

RealScout CEO Andrew Flachner framed the move as a transparency play, with a not-so-subtle shot at private listing networks.

Industry observers note that “Listing transparency comes down to whether a buyer can choose the agent they trust without worrying that the right home is hiding behind another brokerage’s velvet rope,” Flachner noted in a statement. “With Zillow Preview listings from hundreds of brokerages now available in RealScout, agents can give their clients more of the market through the home search experience they already share.”.

For agents, the integration means clients can see pre-MLS listings from participating brokerages in the search tool they already use, without signing up for Zillow or leaving the agent relationship. It also gives buyer’s agents an earlier look at upcoming inventory, which matters most in tight markets, where a few days’ head start can decide who gets a showing first.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 17:44 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

Microsoft Corp.’s official Python package for its Agent Framework artificial intelligence agent toolkit was compromised earlier this week, as an attacker published two malicious versions to the Python Package Index that were designed to steal cloud and developer credentials.

Recent findings suggest that the malicious versions, 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, were published on Tuesday through Microsoft’s own publisher account, giving them the appearance of a routine patch to a package that sees close to 200,000 downloads a month. Both versions were pulled from PyPI within about an hour, but anyone who installed them in that window is at risk.

In a recent development, researchers at cloud security company Wiz Inc. have since found that the attacker appears to have gained publishing access using a client certificate and private key for Microsoft’s Engineering System Release Pipeline, an internal service the company uses to sign and publish packages. Address filtering on the service blocked the attacker’s first attempt from Amazon Web Services, according to Wiz, though the attacker was able to publish on a second try from Microsoft-owned address space.

How the attacker obtained the credentials is not known. Microsoft had not responded to a request for comment from BleepingComputer as of Wednesday.

The researchers also observed part of the operation, as the attacker’s tooling was reporting its progress to the same public webhook it was using to collect stolen data. The tooling identified itself as Cairn, an open-source penetration-testing framework that uses AI.

The malware itself is delivered through a .pth file added to both releases, a type of file Python runs every time it starts, meaning the credential stealer runs even if the framework itself is never imported. The two versions also kept the genuine agent-framework-core 1.26.0 as a dependency, so the framework continued to work normally while the malware ran in the background.

It has been revealed that once running, the malware collects secrets from environment variables and from other running processes, along with credential files for services such as Azure, npm, Git, Docker and Hugging Face. It also requests Azure managed identity tokens for 12 resources, according to application security manufacturer Endor Labs Inc., with the second version adding requests for GitHub Actions tokens. The stolen data is then compressed, encoded and sent to a webhook.site address controlled by the attacker.

Researchers at malware tracking site OpenSourceMalware described the malware as a “focused credential and token stealer, not a remote access trojan,” noting that it does not install any persistence on infected systems.

According to recent reports, wiz’s analysis suggests the number of victims may be small, though it covers only the 50 requests the attacker’s free webhook.site account retained. Of those, 17 represented only three unique successful thefts of victim data, with the rest coming from the attacker’s own machines and from sandbox and security vendor scanning.

Industry observers note that the incident is not the first this year involving an official Microsoft Python package. In May, Microsoft’s durabletask package was hijacked after its PyPI token was stolen in an attack that has been linked to TeamPCP, the group also behind the compromise of LiteLLM. Wiz states it has not linked the two incidents.

Anyone who installed either of the malicious versions is being urged to treat it as a credential compromise, according to researchers, who recommend rebuilding from version 1.26.0 and rotating any secrets the affected systems could access.

“A list of dependencies in production might show no trace of the framework, while a build runner could have installed it and been shut down before the alert arrived,” James Matchett, head of security at software supply chain security firm Cloudsmith Ltd., told SiliconANGLE.

“If that runner had access to a deployment token, the team needs to know which version it installed and what the token could access,” he added.

Shiba Inu fell to a rare low of $0.0000037 as cryptocurrencies tumbled over the weekend. This low marked the lowest seen in years, going back to 2021, as it fell below the $0.000004 level, which has served as support since the start of 2026.

Last week’s bruising selloff following a tougher interest-rate outlook and a risk-off mood deepened the gloom around the cryptocurrency.

Shiba Inu fell for four straight days in the past week, dropping to a low of $0.0000037 on November 14, 2026, coinciding with the first death cross on its daily chart in 2026.

It has been revealed that at the time of writing, Shiba Inu was down 3.36% in the last 24 hours to $0.00000386 as the crypto market selloff intensified, with a total of $203.7 million liquidated. Mazrael, a long-time Shiba Inu community member and SHIB developer, reacted to the token's latest price weakness with a simple message: "1 SHIB is always 1 SHIB" in response to an X user who pointed out Shiba Inu's price drop.

@Yamoshi160 1 shib is always 1 shib.

Sources indicate that the phrase, often used in the context of Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies during price downturns, serves as a reminder to focus on the unit itself rather than short-term fiat volatility. While a single coin always counts as one unit of the network, the argument against this saying is that fiat value changes amid volatility.

Fed Chairman Kelvin Warsh is set to speak later on Monday on the impact of technology on productivity and jobs, potentially triggering volatility in the markets. The Federal Reserve’s minutes from its October meeting, where it left rates unchanged, will be released Wednesday. Markets have largely priced in a quarter percentage point hike in December.

While the Shiba Inu price is trading in the red, the SHIB burn rate is up 1922%, with 136.81 million SHIB sent to dead wallets in the last 24 hours.

In a recent development, 155.03 million SHIB have been burned in the last seven days, with the weekly burn rate up 14.40%. 395.10 million SHIB worth $1753 was burned in the last 30 days, although the burn rate was down 55.45% in the time frame.

A total of 410,845,352,742,359 SHIB has been burned in 21,967 transactions, contributing to 41.08% of the total supply.

"USD Duration is 3.4 yrs and STRC's BTC Credit tightened to 67 bps (-3 bps), assuming 10% BTC ARR, 40% BTC Vol, and a BTC price of $68,800," Saylor added.

The unrealized loss of the organization on its Bitcoin holdings stands at around $9.8 billion. On Sunday, when the price of Bitcoin fell to $62,029 on Bitfinex, the loss was above $11 billion.

Existing-home sales sink to a 16-year low as mortgage rates bite

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • October was the perfect storm for existing-home sales, with a typical seasonal slowdown made worse by elevated mortgage rates, a worsening macroeconomic environment and political uncertainty.
  • According to recent reports, existing-home sales during October declined 5.5 percent month-over-month and 8.8 percent year-over-year to a seasonally adjusted rate of 3.75 million, the lowest rate since August 2010 (3.68 million).
  • Despite slowing sales, unsold inventory (1.59 million units) and the median home price ($416,700) increased by 1.3 percent and 0.4 percent, respectively.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

October was the perfect storm for existing-home sales, with a typical seasonal slowdown made worse by elevated mortgage rates, a worsening macroeconomic environment and political uncertainty.

According to recent reports, existing-home sales during October declined 5.5 percent month-over-month and 8.8 percent year-over-year to a seasonally adjusted rate of 3.75 million, the lowest rate since August 2010 (3.68 million). Annual sales declined in all four regions; however, the Northeast was the only region to also experience a month-over-month drop.

Despite slowing sales, unsold inventory (1.59 million units) and the median home price ($416,700) increased by 1.3 percent and 0.4 percent, respectively.

NAR Chief Economist Lawrence Yun mentioned mortgage rates are the primary cause of current market woes.

Fixed rates experienced a rapid-fire ascent at the beginning of the fall, breaching 7 percent on Sept. 24 and then roughly a week later reaching a three-year high of 7.40 percent on Oct. 8. The catalyst had been two-fold: the Federal Reserve had hiked the federal funds rate (i.e., short-term rate) by 25 basis points during its Sept. 16 FOMC meeting and 10-year Treasury yields were rising at a historic pace.

Rates have since relaxed to the lower 7 percent range, but the short-term damage is already done.

“Homebuying is difficult when mortgage rates have climbed to their highest levels since 2000, aside from a single month in 2023,” Yun said in a written statement. “As a result, home sales fell to their lowest level since August 2010.”.

Although Freddie Mac’s Primary Mortgage Market Survey saw rates drop for the fourth consecutive week to 7.11 percent, Bright MLS Chief Economist Lisa Sturtevant said she expects mortgage rates to start rising again in the coming weeks because of sticky inflation.

“There is little reason to expect rates to come down before the end of the year,” Sturtevant noted in an emailed statement. “In fact, given this week’s inflation report, it is much more likely for us to see rates increase instead of decrease.”.

Yun and Sturtevant noted mortgage rates will continue to impact home sales — not inventory and home price growth.

“So far, we haven’t seen higher rates lead to widespread price declines. In fact, home prices are still rising in many local markets,” Sturtevant said. “Inventory is rising, but higher rates are holding back some sellers along with buyers. Because both sides of the supply-demand equation are slowing, it’s not likely for home prices to drop significantly, even if rates move higher.”.

In a recent development, added Yun, “It will be the highest inventory count since November 2019. We are now back to pre-COVID inventory conditions.”.

Mortgage rate volatility has pushed homebuyers to slow down or pull out of the market altogether, as shown by September’s pending home sales, which declined 7.3 percent month over month and 11.3 percent year over year.

It has been revealed that as a result, homes are sitting on the market longer, averaging 35 days. Most homesellers, Yun remarked, can wait for the market to turn in their favor, thanks to strong home price appreciation.

“Despite fewer transactions in October, the 88 million homeowners across the country are largely in a comfortable financial position due to sizable housing wealth accumulation,” he said. “The number of distressed property sales remains historically low at only 2 percent of all transactions.”.

However, if a homeseller is in the position where they have to sell now, due to career or family changes, they’ll need to get comfortable with making a price cut.

Industry observers note that “If the homes are not selling at the listing price, it requires a discount,” Yun remarked in a pre-report call Thursday morning. “The longer the days on market, the larger the discount. If the home is sitting on the market for more than 60 days, it requires a 9 percent discount … Even with this discount that is occurring, the median home price is still squeaking out a small gain.”.

Yun and Realtor.com Chief Economist Danielle Hale mentioned existing-home sales could improve in November and December — if mortgage rates continue to relax.

According to recent reports, “Fortunately, the 10-year Treasury yield has pulled back from its early October highs, which has helped nudge mortgage rates below this recent peak,” she mentioned. “However, several factors are likely to put a floor under how low rates can go.”.

Hale mentioned jobs and inflation trends will determine whether rates can move back toward the high sixes.

“[The] expected need for tighter monetary policy in the near term combined with sizable demand for capital from both governments and private companies, largely to finance AI-related investments [also matter],” she said. “Put simply, I expect to see more homebuyers come back into the market as we move away from recent mortgage rate highs, but the upside will be limited.”.

Yun stated rates below 7 percent could unleash a wave of untapped demand, allowing homebuyers to finally seize the advantage they’ve been given in terms of income growth, inventory and negotiating power.

Industry observers note that “One wonders whether current price-declining markets will see buyers step in and stabilize the market,” he said. “We are not in a recession, and we are adding jobs. First part is prices, second is income growth. Wage growth is helping modestly on home affordability, but the big change is from mortgage rates. If mortgage rates can come down under 7 percent, we’ll see whether we see more buyer traffic.”.

It has been revealed that however, Sturtevant is less bullish on mortgage rates, noting that rate shifts don’t guarantee buyers the affordability break they seek. The Bright MLS economist pointed to the fact that home prices have continued rising in many markets, despite rates exceeding 7 percent.

“There is little reason to expect rates to come down further this year,” she said. “In fact, given this week’s inflation report, it is much more likely for us to see rates increase instead of decrease. Data on new pending contracts, showing activity and buyer traffic suggest that sales are going to continue to be anemic in the 4th quarter. It is very likely we will end 2026 with a total of fewer than 4 million existing home sales for the first time since the 1990s.”.

The Rise of the House Manager: Why Busy Families Are Outsourcing Everyday Tasks

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Between managing the demands of work and keeping up with everything at home, it can feel like there are never enough hours in the day.
  • For busy, overscheduled families, hiring a house manager may be the key to reclaiming valuable time, reducing daily stress, and bringing a little more balance to everyday life.
  • For those who are unfamiliar with this trending form of home support, a house manager is basically someone who keeps track of things behind the scenes so you can off-load some of your never-ending to-do list.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Between managing the demands of work and keeping up with everything at home, it can feel like there are never enough hours in the day.

For busy, overscheduled families, hiring a house manager may be the key to reclaiming valuable time, reducing daily stress, and bringing a little more balance to everyday life.

For those who are unfamiliar with this trending form of home support, a house manager is basically someone who keeps track of things behind the scenes so you can off-load some of your never-ending to-do list.

It has been revealed that "A house manager takes on the parts of the household a family chooses to hand off—that means both the everyday work and the planning behind it, from start to finish," says Kelly Hubbell, founder and CEO of Sage Haus, a thriving house manager placement company. "Think meals, laundry, errands, calendars, pet care, and home projects. A house manager doesn't just complete tasks ... they anticipate what's needed and handle it without being asked.".

In other words, a house manager is an added support system that helps keep a household functioning efficiently.

The simplest definition of a house manger is someone who helps facilitate everyday life behind the scenes.

"A housekeeper cleans, a nanny cares for the kids, a house manager owns whole areas of the household, from planning to follow-through," says Hubbell.

In a recent development, there can be overlap. A house manager might tidy, do laundry, or prepare meals, depending on what the family hands off. The difference is ownership.

"Take laundry: A housekeeper might wash what's in the basket, whereas a house manager who owns laundry knows the soccer uniform has to be clean by Saturday, without a reminder," explains Hubbell. "The work that's different is the thinking behind the household.".

The best house managers have sharp judgment and the ability to proposal ahead, juggle several schedules and tasks at once, manage vendors, and make good decisions within the scope a family has agreed to, according to Hubbell.

They're proactive and notice what needs attention before anyone asks. And because they're in someone's home, trust, reliability, and discretion are essential.

"People come to it from lots of backgrounds: nannies whose kids aged out of needing a nanny, teachers, hospitality and operations managers, military spouses who have set up a household in four cities, and moms coming back into the workforce after years of running their own homes—frankly, the hardest training there is," says Hubbell, whose network now includes over 7,000 house managers in the U.S. and Canada, though Sage Haus accepts only about 5% of applicants to ensure quality.

"As AI changes the jobs available, this work depends on what technology can't supply: human judgment, trust, and care," she explains.

Basically, house managers are gaining traction because people are burning out, especially women.

In a recent development, "Most families hit a point where their life, career, or ambitions can't grow any further without more support—I call that the support ceiling," says Hubbell. "They don't need to scale back their dreams. They need to scale up their support.".

Many families already have some help, like a cleaner every other week, a nanny/sitter, or groceries on autopilot. But someone still has to hold it all together—the noticing, planning, and following up.

"That's the mental load, and research shows it usually stays with mom, even as her career and earnings grow," indicates Hubbell.

Industry observers note that according to a 2024 study from the University of Bath and the University of Melbourne, mothers in the U.S. carry 71% of mental-load tasks, and while women’s employment and earnings reduce their physical household labor, it does not shrink their cognitive burden.

"Real estate has always recognized the value of a well-maintained home. What we're only beginning to recognize is the value of the work required to maintain it," says Laura Marie Rivera, a gender equity and unpaid labor researcher and host of the "Motherhood Advantage" podcast. "The rise of professional house managers puts a job title and salary on responsibilities that mothers have managed for generations—largely without either.".

Sources indicate that unpaid household work in the U.S. is worth up to $6 trillion a year, and none of it shows up in the GDP. However, the rise of house mangers is finally putting a dollar amount on the mental load of keeping a home operational.

"Paying someone to manage a household doesn't just reveal the economic value of the work, it reveals the scope of the work," says Rivera. "We're not witnessing the invention of a latest profession so much as the professional recognition of work that has been hiding in plain sight.".

The good news is that having a house manager isn't only for the wealthy. In general, cost depends on where you live and what you need the house manager to take on.

"Families hire and pay house managers directly, and pay ranges from $25 to more than $50 an hour depending on location and scope," indicates Hubbell. "It doesn't have to be full time: 80% of families start with part-time help, averaging 15 to 20 hours per week.".

For many families, a house manager can be a more practical investment than several separate kinds of help, because it brings that support together in one role. However, there are still options when budgetary constraints prohibit the employment of a house manager.

"Support doesn't have to start with a hire," claims Hubbell. "It can begin with mapping out everything it takes to run your home and deciding what to drop, what to share with a partner, and where you need help most.".

That being said, for those who can swing it, having a house manager can be life-changing.

In theory this all sounds amazing, but what's it like in practice? We checked in with a house manager and a family that's hired a house manager to get the inside scoop. But the short version is, both are very happy with their decision.

Before becoming a house manager, Terry Boch worked as an executive assistant, but also spent years as a stay-at-home mom raising her three children.

Recent findings suggest that once they were grown and she reentered the work force, she was enjoying being an executive assistant again but realized she wanted something less computer-focused and more hands-on. That's when she came across a job post seeking house managers. Intrigued, she pursued the opportunity, was matched with a family in Newly introduced Jersey, and found it was a perfect fit for her skill set.

It has been revealed that "I love transforming an already beautiful house into a warm, welcoming home that looks and smells inviting every day," indicates Boch, whose primary responsibilities include meal planning, grocery shopping and meal preparation, laundry, resetting bedrooms and living spaces, and plant care. "I work approximately 15–20 hours per week, but I like to say that I get to play house in a home I could never afford.".

In reality, however, Boch says she sees what she does as much more about creating a home than maintaining a house.

Industry observers note that "Although my interaction with the children is limited, knowing that I can contribute to an environment where they feel comfortable, cared for, and happy brings me tremendous joy," says Boch. "I love making a home feel welcoming, anticipating what a family needs, and taking pride in all the little things that make everyday life more enjoyable. I'm not a house cleaner; I'm a homemaker at heart.".

On the flip side, Krissel Varela found her way to the idea of hiring a house manager online.

"Following Sage Haus on social media really opened my eyes to what household support could look like," claims Varela. "I had always thought about help in a more traditional sense, like a nanny or someone full-time, but started realizing we could shape the support around what our family actually needed.".

Though she'd had a nanny when her kids were younger and she was working a corporate job, once they reached school age, they didn't need that kind of assistance anymore. However, their lives didn't get less busy.

"Between school, sports, activities, keeping our household running, and now building a business of my own, there are just so many moving pieces," notes Varela. The idea of a house manager made sense for her family, though they didn't need someone full time.

According to recent reports, "Right now, we have help about 8 to 10 hours a week, and even though that's not a huge number of hours, the impact feels so much bigger," says Varela. Her house manager is usually with them on Mondays and Thursdays, with some flexibility predicated on their needs.

"Between laundry, household organization, errands, and all those little tasks that add up throughout the week, having someone share those responsibilities makes such a difference," she adds.

Though it's been only a few months, Varela claims she can already feel a huge life shift.

Sources indicate that "It's not just the actual hours saved; it's also the mental space that comes from knowing someone else is helping keep things moving without having to manage every little detail," indicates Varela. "It's also given me more room for the things that are easy to push aside when life gets busy, whether that's spending quality time with my husband, enjoying our weekends, or even having a little time for myself. Having that extra support has really helped me be more intentional about where my time and energy go.".

And that is exactly what a house manager is supposed to do, open up space for life at home to be about more than just getting by every day.

"People should also know there's a cost to getting support and a cost to going without it, whether that's your health, your relationships, or your connection with your family," claims Hubbell. "The goal isn't to outsource your life; it's to get enough support to be present for it.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The latest model, confirmed Wednesday, reflects the tech giant’s argument that while AI has transformed how software gets written, it has barely touched how software gets run.
  • SRE-1 is a 27 billion-parameter model built on open weights and trained by a team of 16 AI researchers over a final run of 7.4 days on up to 512 graphics processing units.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 18:11 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

Recent findings suggest that incident remediation firm Resolve AI Inc. has confirmed the launch of SRE-1, a newly introduced model that has been trained to find the root cause of production alerts, and Primary On-call, a new service that puts its artificial intelligence agents on call ahead of human engineers.

The latest model, confirmed Wednesday, reflects the tech giant’s argument that while AI has transformed how software gets written, it has barely touched how software gets run. According to Resolve AI, production has no public training corpus to match the published code that models learned from, as incidents at each company stay private.

SRE-1 is a 27 billion-parameter model built on open weights and trained by a team of 16 AI researchers over a final run of 7.4 days on up to 512 graphics processing units. Measured on the same incidents before and after training, which used reinforcement learning alone, the pass rate for a single investigation rose from 6.9% to 38.8%.

Industry observers note that resolve AI used Snowflake Inc.’s Cortex Training, a serverless service for customizing open-weight models, to build SRE-1. Snowflake Senior Vice President of Engineering Vivek Raghunathan said Resolve AI was the first design partner for the service.

It has been revealed that in testing on 49 difficult live production cases, each run five times, an ensemble of five SRE-1 investigations matched the strongest frontier model tested at a lower cost, according to the tech giant. Resolve AI also benchmarked its complete system on 178 production alert investigations, solving about twice as many incidents as general-purpose coding agents.

Industry observers note that primary On-call puts that research to work on the critical path. Each page is investigated across telemetry, infrastructure, code and operational knowledge, according to the company. Depending on what it finds, the agent can close the alert, mitigate the problem where a team’s policies permit or escalate to a human. Once it has acted, the agent checks the fix against the production baseline, monitoring it until recovery holds.

The agent also links related alerts and investigations into a shared view of each underlying problem. For teams wary of handing over the pager straight away, Resolve AI offers a shadow mode that records the call the agent would have made on each page.

According to recent reports, up to 80% of paged alerts in production are noted to be handled by Primary On-call without escalation. Customers have reported a tenfold improvement in mean time to resolution, along with root-cause accuracy of up to 95%, according to Resolve AI.

Salesforce Inc. is among the early customers. Bhupesh Patel, a software engineering principal architect at Salesforce, remarked that in the first few weeks of dark launch testing, the agent closed more than 70% of the CRM Analytics team’s paging alerts “without waking an engineer.”.

“No engineering team can keep up with how fast code and patches land in production,” noted Resolve AI Chief Executive Spiros Xanthos. “The answer is agents that are accurate and fast enough to sit on the critical path, and that takes a model built for production.”.

Sources indicate that primary On-call is now generally available. Access to SRE-1 is limited to Resolve AI’s own platform.

Resolve AI is a venture capital-backed startup that has raised more than $190 million to date, including a $40 million extension to its Series A round in April, led by DST Global and Salesforce Ventures, that valued the company at $1.5 billion. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Authorities in the United States and Canada have revealed a major cross-border crackdown on cryptocurrency fraud, bringing together law enforcement agencies, financial regulators and private companies to target online scam networks.
  • The Ontario Securities Commission (OSC) unveiled on Nov.
  • According to the Canadian securities regulator, the operation involves investigators, securities specialists and financial crime experts from both countries.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Authorities in the United States and Canada have revealed a major cross-border crackdown on cryptocurrency fraud, bringing together law enforcement agencies, financial regulators and private companies to target online scam networks.

The Ontario Securities Commission (OSC) unveiled on Nov. 16 the launch of Operation Niagara, a coordinated initiative aimed at disrupting organized cryptocurrency fraud schemes and protecting potential victims.

According to the Canadian securities regulator, the operation involves investigators, securities specialists and financial crime experts from both countries.

The initiative will use advanced technology and enhanced investigative capabilities to identify fraudulent activity and potential victims in near real time.

Importantly, the operation will not focus solely on investigating criminals after fraud has occurred. Authorities also intend to identify individuals who are being targeted by scammers and intervene before they suffer further financial losses.

"Fraud knows no border, and it targets everyday people," said Bonnie Lysyk, Executive Vice-President of Enforcement at the OSC.

The initiative brings together several major law enforcement and regulatory agencies, including the U.S. Secret Service, Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) and Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP).

Canadian securities regulators, including the Alberta Securities Commission, British Columbia Securities Commission and Autorité des marchés financiers, are also participating.

Private-sector companies will contribute technical expertise and intelligence to help authorities identify and disrupt fraudulent networks.

It’s worth noting that the OSC didn’t provide details on how many fraud networks it is targeting, how many potential victims have been identified or how much cryptocurrency is involved in Operation Niagara.

#41975. October Marks the First Month in 3 Years With a Decline in U.S. Home-Sale Prices

📅 10 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1026 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Redfin ↗ Open Full Page

October Marks the First Month in 3 Years With a Decline in U.S. Home-Sale Prices

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1026 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Redfin

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • home-sale prices rose from a year earlier every single month, even as mortgage rates climbed and would-be buyers pulled back.
  • Recent findings suggest that the median home-sale price declined 0.4% year over year to $388,634 in October.
  • With the total number of homes for sale at its highest level since early 2020 and demand cooling, homebuyers’ negotiating power keeps increasing–and that’s finally showing up in sale prices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For three years, U.S. home-sale prices rose from a year earlier every single month, even as mortgage rates climbed and would-be buyers pulled back. That streak has ended.

Recent findings suggest that the median home-sale price declined 0.4% year over year to $388,634 in October. That’s  the first decline since May 2023 and a sharp slowdown from the 2.5% gain just two months earlier. With Americans’ wages growing about 4% year over year, even a slight dip in prices can improve affordability. Sale prices have risen nearly every single month for the last 13 years; the only exception was a handful of months in 2023.

With the total number of homes for sale at its highest level since early 2020 and demand cooling, homebuyers’ negotiating power keeps increasing–and that’s finally showing up in sale prices.

According to recent reports, home-sale prices fell nationwide, but they rose in more than half of the 50 most populous U.S. metro areas. San Francisco led the nation by a wide margin, with the median sale price rising 16.8% year over year. That’s the biggest increase since 2018. Next comes Newly introduced Brunswick, NJ, with a 7.7% gain. Two other NYC-area metros also had price increases ranking in the top six; the median sale price rose 4.4% in both New York City and Nassau County.

In San Francisco, AI wealth is fueling competition for scarce inventory; active listings were down 7% from a year earlier. In the Newly introduced York City area, years of limited homebuilding have left buyers competing for relatively few homes in a region with a strong job market.

Home-sale prices fell most in Austin, TX, where they declined 6.5% year over year. It’s followed by Seattle (-5.1%) and Nashville, TN (-4.9%). Austin and Nashville are among the biggest buyer’s markets in the U.S., and Seattle’s shaky tech job market is curbing demand.

According to recent reports, national sale prices are losing steam because fewer Americans can afford to buy a home. U.S. pending home sales fell 3.6% from a month earlier in October on a seasonally adjusted basis to their lowest level since 2013, with the exception of April 2020.

This is a real-time indicator of the state of the housing market; fewer homes went under contract in October largely because mortgage rates averaged 7.33%, a three-year high and up from 6.86% the month before.

All figures in this report are seasonally adjusted, with the exception of median sale price data and mortgage rate data. See a more detailed methodology here and view an interactive dashboard here.

In a recent development, “It’s a buyer’s market, but not many people can afford to buy,” remarked Chen Zhao, Redfin’s head of economics. “That could start to shift a bit, now that sale prices are closer to reflecting the shape of the market. House hunters in most of the country should know that the price they see on a listing may very well be a starting point; they should try offering below the asking price, and negotiating for closing costs, repairs and maybe even mortgage-rate buydowns. If you can’t get the price or monthly payment you want on one house, move on to the next one–with a major pool of inventory sitting on the market, buyers can afford to be picky.”.

Pending home sales declined in all of the most populous U.S. metros. That’s the second month in a row that has happened; before September, the last time was three years earlier.

Industry observers note that the biggest declines were in Seattle and San Diego, both places where pending sales fell more than 20% year over year. Those West Coast metros are some of the priciest in the U.S., so 7%-plus mortgages hit house hunters’ monthly payments there hard. In Seattle, an uncertain local job market is also curbing demand.

According to recent reports, closed home sales fell to their lowest level in nearly 3 years. They declined 2.1% month over month in October to their lowest level since December 2023; before that, the last time sales dropped that low was 2014. Many of the deals that closed last month went under contract in August and September, when rates were already climbing and economic uncertainty was deterring a lot of house hunters.

Industry observers note that with homebuying demand falling, supply is building. The total number of homes for sale rose 0.9% from September to its highest level since early 2020; that’s the biggest monthly gain since May 2025.

More supply gives buyers more homes to choose from and more leverage:.

“Buyers are nervous about rates, the economy, and everything they’re seeing in the news– so they need the house and the price to line up perfectly before they’ll make an offer,” noted Callie Kimmel, a Redfin Premier agent in Philadelphia. “I’m advising sellers to price just below current market value from day one–and not comps from six months ago, but homes that are listed right now. Otherwise, the home is likely to end up sitting on the market for a bit and selling for less than they hoped. There are a few exceptions: Move-in ready homes in the most desirable neighborhoods are still competitive; in those cases, sellers have the upper hand.”.

While total housing supply is growing, fewer sellers are adding latest inventory to the pool. New listings of homes for sale fell 1% month over month to the lowest level in more than two years. Would-be sellers are pulling back as homebuying demand slows and sale prices lose steam.

The figures below are based on a list of the 50 most populous U.S. metropolitan areas. Some metros may be removed from time to time to ensure data accuracy. Refer to our metrics definition page for explanations of metrics used in this report. All changes below represent year-over-year changes.

As a data journalist at Redfin, Dana Anderson writes about the numbers behind real estate trends. Although the bank did not disclose the specific amount it had invested in the asset, the filing has triggered discussions as it highlights XRP’s growing exposure among institutional investors.

Unlike regular investors who purchase XRP directly from exchanges and hold in their wallets, the bank invested in XRP through Bitwise's fund.

With its XRP ETF offering, Bitwise allows traditional investors to gain exposure to XRP without having to manage the crypto asset themselves.

Although XRP has continued to see major institutions and banks join its ETF ecosystem, participation in the XRP funds have slowed significantly following the ongoing market volatility.

While the exposure showcased by the major Canadian bank shows growing XRP ETF adoption, it doesn’t change the fact that institutional traders are beginning to take caution as they have just recorded the highest weekly withdrawals since March 2026.

The bank’s XRP exposure has triggered discussions as it reveals that it has retained its position till September 30 despite the persisting market correction.

Despite posting a solid earnings beat, Elastic sees its stock slide on rough guidance

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (967 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Elastic N.V.’s stock was trending lower in late trading today after the enterprise search software firm reported earnings and revenue that beat Wall Street’s expectations but disappointed with guidance that came in below forecasts.
  • Industry observers note that the tech giant reported second-quarter earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of 94 cents per share, easily beating the analyst consensus estimate of 81 cents.
  • The results helped Elastic bounce back into profitability.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 18:33 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

Elastic N.V.’s stock was trending lower in late trading today after the enterprise search software firm reported earnings and revenue that beat Wall Street’s expectations but disappointed with guidance that came in below forecasts.

Industry observers note that the tech giant reported second-quarter earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of 94 cents per share, easily beating the analyst consensus estimate of 81 cents. Revenue rose 17%, to $496 million, surpassing the Street’s target of $487 million.

The results helped Elastic bounce back into profitability. Its net income for the quarter came to $171 million, rebounding from a loss of $51.3 million in the same period one year ago.

It has been revealed that however, investors were less than impressed with the tech giant’s guidance. For the quarter in progress, Elastic remarked it’s looking for earnings of between 90 cents and 92 cents per share on sales of $507.5 million to $508.5 million. That’s some way below the Street’s targets of 95 cents in earnings and $517.6 million in revenue. The company is not helped by the weak Euro, with currency conversions likely to cause a $4.5 million headwind on revenue in the quarter.

The full-year picture is not much better, as Elastic forecast annual sales of between $2 billion and $2.01 billion compared with the Street’s model of $2.01 billion.

Netherlands-based Elastic is one of Europe’s most successful software companies. It’s the developer of the popular open-source enterprise search platform Elasticsearch, which is used by thousands of businesses all over the world. The base platform is free to download and use, with Elastic making money by selling a special cloud-hosted version that ships with premium features not available in the open edition. The tech giant also sells application observability and security tools.

In a recent development, in the last couple of years, Elastic has tried to cash in on the artificial intelligence boom by positioning Elasticsearch as a useful cog in the wheel that feeds real-time data into large language models to provide them with business context. A key capability is Elastic Context Engine, which gathers, structures, and serves business-specific context to AI agents so they can make accurate decisions with fewer tokens and lower latency.

More recently, the organization has built AI-native products including AlertZero, which enables enterprises to orchestrate teams of autonomous security agents that automate tasks around data protection and threat hunting.

Elastic Chief Executive Ash Kulkarni (pictured) said he’s excited about the potential of those newly introduced capabilities to drive significant revenue over time. “Elastic delivered another strong quarter, beating guidance across all key metrics,” he said. “Our strong results reflect expanding customer adoption and position us well to continue our strong execution in the back half of fiscal 2027.”.

Unfortunately for Kulkarni, investors didn’t seem to share his enthusiasm. The market was clearly expecting trouble on the horizon in the hours before the company published its report, as its stock declined 8% during regular trading. Once the results were out, it fell another 8% after-hours. That means Elastic’s stock is now up just over 1% in the year to date.

Elastic’s stock had rallied more than 150% between April and October, but virtually all of those gains have now been erased. Prior to today, the shares had already lost more than 20% this month amid broader concerns about the AI industry. Some investors continue to worry about the potential of AI technology to challenge the business models of software companies.

Elastic is trying to sidestep those concerns by de-emphasizing search and observability and moving towards runtime context, model evaluation and AI operations, but investors are not yet convinced it will be able to do so successfully, Constellation Research analyst Michael Ni told SiliconANGLE.

“While Elastic is showing good underlying momentum, the Street wants to see more proof that its re-acceleration can hold,” Ni stated. “The next few quarters will show whether the broader platform story translates into sustainable growth or remains ahead of the numbers.”.

  • The AI wealth boom was in the spotlight this week, following Anthropic’s highly anticipated IPO and jaw dropping $1.494 trillion valuation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The artificial intelligence boom has expanded from the rolling hills of San Francisco and Silicon Valley to the busy streets of Newly introduced York City, where an already tight luxury market is feeling the impact.

The AI wealth boom was in the spotlight this week, following Anthropic’s highly anticipated IPO and jaw dropping $1.494 trillion valuation. With the tech constantly growing and producing newly minted millionaires, the impacts of deep-pocketed AI professionals entering the Newly introduced York real estate market are just beginning to be felt, agents there say.

There are more than 2,000 AI companies operating in Upcoming York City, according to the city’s Economic Development Corporation, and AI companies signed leases for about 1.5 million square feet in just the first six months of 2026, the Brooklyn Daily Eagle reported.

Major AI frontrunners like Anthropic, Palantir, OpenAI, and EliseAI have opened offices in Upcoming York, contributing to the thriving commercial real estate market.

“It’s been pretty unbelievable, what’s happening in the public sphere of the AI business. We’re seeing a ton of AI leasing activity on the ground in Latest York,” Evan Kleinberg, co-founder of Cornelia Street Partners, a boutique commercial real estate firm, told Realtor.com. “And it’s been happening so fast, it’s almost representative of the technology itself. The companies hire immediately and they need space yesterday.”.

While Kleinberg has been keeping eyes on the AI industry for the past couple of years, his brokerage worked with its first AI specific company about 12 months ago, at the end of 2025. Since then, the brokerage has secured leases for five companies developing proprietary AI models.

There are a number of reasons Kleinberg sees AI companies expanding east and planting roots in New York. The city has fully rebounded from the pandemic and has an attractive lifestyle that draws many young professionals. Plus, companies see the benefit of being close to their portfolio businesses.

In a recent development, “Ultimately, if your goal is to raise money from Goldman Sachs or JP Morgan or one of the major private equity groups like Apollo, they’re all here,” Kleinberg explained. “So wanting to get close to them is an underlying reason to move.”.

With these upcoming offices comes a hoard of young, newly wealthy professionals who are looking to build a home in New York, many of whom are stepping into an already fiercely competitive luxury real estate market.

“Wall Street has historically been a major driver of Manhattan luxury real estate, and now we’re really starting to see the effects of AI. It’s becoming an vital engine for wealth creation and housing demand,” Michelle Griffith, a residential real estate agent in Newly introduced York City, told Realtor.com. “Right now in Manhattan, we are already in a very tight rental market. Even for the last year, rents are up anywhere from 10% to 20% in Manhattan, especially for these luxury properties.”.

It has been revealed that as of November, the median sold price of a home in Manhattan is $1,150,000, a 15% year over year increase. Some Manhattan neighborhoods have had more extreme changes.

The Lower East Side, for example, saw the median sale price jump 28% year over year to $1,435,000. Rent in the Lower East Side also increased 11% year over year, for a median of $5,947 per month.

It has been revealed that the Newly introduced York City luxury residential landscape is no stranger to competition, with deep pocketed masses vying for a severely limited inventory of spaces. With the flood of AI professionals, another layer of people has been added to the market.

Sources indicate that griffith recalled a recent listing at 50 Gramercy Park North, which had historically rented for $30,000. While a rental like this, which is in the higher end of the market, would previously take 30 to 60 days to identify a tenant, the listing had eight rental bids after 48 hours on the market, with half above asking.

Most workers are determined to live close to work, making it especially challenging to secure an apartment in these highly sought after neighborhoods.

OpenAI’s 90,000-square-foot New York office is located in the Puck Building, which sits on the boarder of SoHo and Nolita in Manhattan.

Anthropic’s Latest York hub takes up the entirety of a 16-story building at 330 Hudson Street in the Hudson Square neighborhood of Lower Manhattan.

It has been revealed that “The offices are in fantastic locations, so it’s easy to find great housing within walking distance,” said Griffith. “The challenge is finding that apartment because there is very, very limited inventory because those neighborhoods were already popular and in demand.”.

For luxury agents, the challenge is no longer finding tenants with the money to rent high priced rentals, its finding the rentals for deep pocketed tenants.

When Griffith began in real estate 15 years ago, an apartment for $100,000 per month might be the biggest rental of the year. Now, rentals for $80,000 to even $150,000 are common and moving swiftly, she shared.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • What do door-to-door Bible salesmen have to do with luxury real estate?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What do door-to-door Bible salesmen have to do with luxury real estate? For Wade Shealy, everything.

It has been revealed that on this episode of Real Estate Insiders Unfiltered, James Dwiggins and Keith Robinson sit down with Shealy, founder and CEO of ThirdHome, the luxury home exchange club he started in 2010 with just two homes. Today it has more than 35,000 homes in over 100 countries. Shealy shares how selling Bibles and dictionaries door to door paid his way through the University of Georgia and how it led him to Hilton Head in 1984 to a career in resort real estate.

He explains why second homeowners kept coming back within five years wanting to sell and how that pattern became the idea for ThirdHome. He also walks through how he signed up his first 1,500 members and how the club’s key system works. Plus, he shares the biggest lesson he’s learned from his partner, Mrs. Fields founder Debbi Fields: Make everyone you meet feel important.

They also get into handling rejection, taking major risks and why Shealy believes very few people will buy a vacation home without a home exchange membership 10 years from now.

Shealy explains the luxury home exchange club model simply. Owners deposit unused weeks in their second home and earn credits called keys. They use those keys to book stays in other members’ homes, paying only an exchange fee of around $900 instead of thousands in rent. The club has now completed 100,000 exchanges, and Shealy states many members who would never rent out their home happily exchange it.

Recent findings suggest that for agents, Shealy points to ThirdHome’s ambassador program. In Cabo San Lucas, developers began offering ThirdHome access as part of their sales pitch, and the club grew to roughly 8,000 properties there. He believes the next generation of buyers will expect mobility and experiences, not just a single vacation home.

Recent findings suggest that his advice for agents: Look at what everyone else is doing, and do the opposite. Above all, keep changing, because if you’re marketing the same way you did 20 years ago, you’re already behind.

#41969. Just 3 Major U.S. Metros Are Seller’s Markets–the Fewest Since the Pandemic Freeze

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1343 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Redfin ↗ Open Full Page

Just 3 Major U.S. Metros Are Seller’s Markets–the Fewest Since the Pandemic Freeze

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1343 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Redfin

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Just three of the 50 most populous U.S.
  • Nassau County, NY was the number-one seller’s market, with 24.7% fewer sellers than buyers.
  • Industry observers note that all three seller’s markets became less strong seller’s markets in October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just three of the 50 most populous U.S. metro areas were seller’s markets in October. That’s tied for the fewest in records dating back to 2016, matching April 2020, when the pandemic froze the housing market.

Nassau County, NY was the number-one seller’s market, with 24.7% fewer sellers than buyers. The other seller’s markets were Newark, NJ (-14.3%) and Montgomery County, PA (-12.1%).

Industry observers note that all three seller’s markets became less strong seller’s markets in October. In Nassau County, there were 28.3% fewer sellers than buyers in September, a bigger gap than October’s 24.7%. Newark’s gap shrunk from 17.6% to 14.3%, and Montgomery County’s shrunk from 20.1% to 12.1%. Milwaukee, which was a seller’s market in September, is now balanced, meaning it doesn’t favor sellers or buyers.

Sources indicate that the seller’s markets are places where limited homebuilding has kept housing supply tight. In the greater New York City area, combine that with strong demand for homes near a major job center, and buyers are competing for homes. Home-sale prices rose an average of 3.3% year over year across the three seller’s markets in October. That’s compared with a 0.3% uptick across all of the buyer’s markets, a sign that in seller’s markets, competition among buyers is pushing up home prices.

“Buyers looking in these pockets of the Northeast should be prepared for a very different experience than buyers elsewhere in the country,” noted Redfin Senior Economist Asad Khan. “They may have less room to negotiate, especially on desirable, move-in-ready homes, and could face multiple-offer situations. If you’re shopping in one of these markets, it’s especially vital to know your budget, be ready to act when the right home comes along and avoid getting swept up in a bidding war.”.

Seller’s markets are the exception to a national picture that heavily favors buyers.

Nationwide, homebuyers have more negotiating power than at any point in Redfin’s records. There were an estimated 70.5% more home sellers than buyers in the U.S. housing market in October, the biggest gap in records dating back to 2013.

That marks the sixth record-breaking month in a row, and the margin is up from 65.6% in September. The Sun Belt is driving the extreme buyer’s market nationwide, led by huge seller surpluses in Miami, Nashville, TN and Las Vegas.

In a recent development, when sellers outnumber buyers, buyers typically have more negotiating power because they have options. That’s why a market with a lot more sellers than buyers is considered a buyer’s market. We define a market where there are over 10% more sellers than buyers as a buyer’s market and a market where there are over 10% fewer sellers than buyers as a seller’s market. A market where the gap is plus or minus 10% is considered a balanced market.

We estimated the number of buyers using proprietary Redfin data on the typical time from a buyer’s first tour to close of purchase, and MLS data on active listings and pending sales. The estimated number of sellers in the market is simply the number of active listings in the MLS. These estimates are seasonally adjusted and subject to revision. See a more detailed methodology here and view an interactive dashboard here.

In a recent development, it’s only a buyer’s market for people who can afford to buy. High housing costs and economic jitters have pushed many would-be homebuyers to back off in recent years, creating the imbalance between buyers and sellers we see today.

“A buyer-friendly market can help make homeownership a little more attainable, even if it doesn’t solve the affordability challenges that have kept many people on the sidelines,” Khan said. “Sellers are increasingly competing for buyers’ attention, which can translate into price reductions, concessions and other savings. First-time buyers don’t have equity from a previous home to put toward a purchase, which makes saving for a down payment a major hurdle–but they also don’t have to sell a home before they can buy or give up a low mortgage rate. With a historic buyer’s market and home prices that are finally ticking down after three years of increases, first-time buyers who have been waiting–and can afford today’s costs–may have an opportunity to make a move.”.

The gap between buyers and sellers widened in October because would-be buyers retreated, while sellers continued listing their homes, albeit at a sluggish pace.

There were an estimated 895,752 homebuyers in the market nationwide in October, the lowest level in records dating back to 2013. That’s down 2% from a month earlier, the sixth straight monthly decline. Mortgage rates averaged 7.33% in October, up from 6.86% in September, which priced out more would-be buyers.

According to recent reports, on the flip side, there were an estimated 1,526,984 home sellers in the market, the most since March 2020. That’s up 0.9% month over month.

In a recent development, the number of homes on the market is piling up because many homes are lingering on the market for months without going under contract. Each month, more new listings are adding to the significant pool of supply.

Recent findings suggest that some homeowners keep listing their houses despite falling demand because many have given up on waiting for lower rates. They may want to sell now because they’re worried prices could decline, and some need to move for a newly introduced job, a growing family, or another life change. But many homeowners who don’t need to move have substantial equity and little pressure to sell, so they may hold off on listing.

It has been revealed that over 80% of U.S. metro areas, 41 of the 50 Redfin analyzed, are buyer’s markets. That matches September’s record.

Recent findings suggest that for the third month in a row, Miami and Nashville have the biggest surpluses of sellers over buyers. Miami had 195.8% more sellers than buyers in October, and Nashville had 159.5% more. Las Vegas (149.9%) was third on the list. In the top 13 buyer’s markets, there were more than twice as many sellers as buyers in October. Nearly all are in the Sun Belt; four are in Texas and four are in Florida.

Sources indicate that the Sun Belt, particularly Texas and Florida, is home to some of the nation’s biggest buyer’s markets, partly because of robust homebuilding. Builders are continuing to add newly introduced homes even as demand cools, swelling inventory and giving buyers more options and negotiating power.

According to recent reports, demand has cooled largely because rising mortgage rates and stubbornly high home prices are pricing buyers out. In Florida, rising HOA and homeowners insurance costs are exacerbating the affordability squeeze.

Six metros were “balanced” in October, neither buyer’s nor seller’s markets: Chicago (8.1% more sellers than buyers), Boston (7.5%), Providence, RI (7.5%), Fresh Brunswick, NJ (5.6%), Milwaukee (0.6% fewer sellers than buyers) and San Francisco (6.9% fewer).

The surplus of home sellers over buyers grew month over month in 34 of the 41 buyer’s markets in October.

It has been revealed that the surplus increased most in Miami, which also has the biggest surplus of sellers over buyers; there were 195.8% more sellers than buyers in October, up from 160.5% the month before. The next-biggest monthly increases were in Las Vegas, where there were 149.9% more sellers than buyers, up from 122.8%, and Nashville (159.5%, up from 134.3%).

Industry observers note that house hunters lost negotiating power in seven buyer’s markets. The surplus of sellers over buyers fell from September to October in Fort Worth, TX (91.6%, down from 100%), St. Louis (23.1%, down from 27.1%), Austin (124.8%, down from 128.2%), Dallas (118.6%, down from 120.5%), Jacksonville, FL, Pittsburgh and Los Angeles. All of them remain buyer’s markets.

As a data journalist at Redfin, Dana Anderson writes about the numbers behind real estate trends.
